optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Software Quality Engineer, Customer Ticketing System

professionalSummary.text: Owns quality for the ticket-routing service end-to-end with two years of experience maintaining automated test suites, release-gate checks, and escaped-defect analysis for weekly releases.
professionalSummary.witness: Responsibilities included test-suite maintenance, release-gate checks, escaped-defect analysis and release quality notes for the ticket-routing service over about two years.

experienceHighlights.text: Maintained automated test suites (unit, contract, load) and release-gate checks, adding a routing-rule regression pack after two escaped defects in rule evaluation.
experienceHighlights.witness: Maintained the ticket-routing service's automated test suites (unit, contract and load) and the release-gate checks in the pipeline, adding a routing-rule regression pack after two escaped defects in rule evaluation.

experienceHighlights.text: Analysed escaped defects fortnightly, recording root causes and prevention actions in the quality log and presenting at engineering reviews.
experienceHighlights.witness: Analysed escaped defects each fortnight, recording root causes and prevention actions in the quality log and presenting them at the engineering review.

experienceHighlights.text: Wrote release quality notes listing known limitations (e.g., load tests not covering enterprise tier rule volumes) and hand-over items for support operations.
experienceHighlights.witness: Wrote the release quality notes for each release, listing known limitations (load tests did not cover the enterprise tier's rule volumes) and the hand-over items for support operations.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Release-gate check configuration and quality log for one quarter with pipeline run identifiers as verification trail.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the release-gate check configuration and the quality log for one quarter, with the pipeline run identifiers as a verification trail.

skills.text: Automated test suite maintenance, release-gate checks, escaped-defect analysis, and release quality documentation.
skills.witness: Responsibilities included test-suite maintenance, release-gate checks, escaped-defect analysis and release quality notes for the ticket-routing service over about two years.

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The materials establish the candidate's experience with test-suite maintenance, release-gate checks, escaped-defect analysis, and release quality notes. They do not establish that the candidate personally held the go/no-go for weekly releases, as the hiring manager's note indicates the release manager 'basically rubber-stamped' the candidate's recommendation.

decisionBoundary.statement: Human review required due to unverified go/no-go ownership claim.

role.roleTitle: Software Quality Engineer, Customer Ticketing System

evidence.text: Responsibilities included test-suite maintenance, release-gate checks, escaped-defect analysis and release quality notes for the ticket-routing service over about two years.
evidence.notes: Covers end-to-end quality ownership but not go/no-go.

evidence.text: Coordinated release scope with the development lead and support operations in the weekly release meeting; the development lead set the scope and the release manager held the go/no-go for each weekly release.
evidence.notes: Confirms release manager held go/no-go, not candidate.

missingEvidence: Candidate personally held go/no-go for weekly releases

evidence.text: Maintained the ticket-routing service's automated test suites (unit, contract and load) and the release-gate checks in the pipeline, adding a routing-rule regression pack after two escaped defects in rule evaluation.
evidence.notes: Direct evidence of test suite and release-gate maintenance.

evidence.text: Work sample: the release-gate check configuration and the quality log for one quarter, with the pipeline run identifiers as a verification trail.
Analysed escaped defects each fortnight, recording root causes and prevention actions in the quality log and presenting them at the engineering review.
Work sample: the release-gate check configuration and the quality log for one quarter, with the pipeline run identifiers as a verification trail.
evidence.notes: Quality log supports root cause recording.

evidence.text: Coordinated release scope with the development lead and support operations in the weekly release meeting; the development lead set the scope and the release manager held the go/no-go for each weekly release.
evidence.notes: Confirms coordination but not candidate's responsibility boundaries.

evidence.text: Wrote the release quality notes for each release, listing known limitations (load tests did not cover the enterprise tier's rule volumes) and the hand-over items for support operations.
evidence.notes: Direct evidence of known limitations and hand-over conditions.

unsupportedClaims.requiredFollowUp: Ask candidate to clarify their role in the go/no-go decision.

missingEvidenceGaps.gap: Candidate personally held go/no-go for weekly releases

interviewSignalRisks.text: the VP of engineering wants a quality engineer who has personally held the weekly go/no-go; in the screen the candidate said the release manager 'basically rubber-stamped what I recommended'.
interviewSignalRisks.recommendedHandling: Verify candidate's role in go/no-go decision during interview.

followUpQuestions.question: Can you describe your role in the go/no-go decision for weekly releases, including how you influenced the decision and whether you personally held the final approval?
How did you document your responsibility boundaries when coordinating release scope with the development lead and support operations?

hiringEvidencePacket.auditSummary: The candidate's materials establish strong evidence for test-suite maintenance, escaped-defect analysis, and release quality notes. However, they do not establish that the candidate personally held the go/no-go for weekly releases, which is a key requirement. The hiring manager's note indicates the release manager rubber-stamped the candidate's recommendation, creating a significant gap. The candidate also did not document responsibility boundaries, a secondary gap. Human review is required to verify these gaps.
limitations: The materials do not establish personal go/no-go ownership
The materials do not establish documentation of responsibility boundaries
